why: He played it at their 8 a.m. weekday wedding, a year to the day after meeting Laura, whom he took for a waitress until she said she owned the place.

cite.t: You know how I said I was taking boxing lessons? Actually, I was doing this. Um, so, I hope that you like it.

q: In “Andy’s Ancestry”, which famous person does Andy believe he is related to?
why: Nellie faked the family tree because she knew Andy would eat it up, and Oscar soon pointed out what the link implied about Andy’s ancestors.

cite.t: My fellow Americans, I have a feeling my approval rating is about to go through the roof. Turns out, I am related to Michelle Obama.

q: In “Work Bus”, what problem in the building forces the office out for a week and onto Dwight’s rented bus?
a: An electromagnetic field from bad wiring
w: A gas leak in the annex
why: Fixing it meant ripping open the walls, and Dwight’s contract as landlord required him to provide a temporary work space.

cite.t: It stands for electromagnetic field. Generally cause by a concentration of wiring in one area Especially if they're poorly insulated. Dwight.

q: In the “Here Comes Treble” cold open, what does Dwight get his head stuck in?
why: He greased his head and hollowed out the pumpkin for a joke on Erin, then claimed any blow to the pumpkin could prove fatal.

cite.t: My greased up head went into the pumpkin no problem, but ...

q: In “The Boat”, who does Andy take with him when he sails off on the family boat?
why: Andy found Walt Jr. on the boat in the middle of a relapse and pitched him three weeks of open ocean with no booze and “serious bro time.”

cite.t: Alright guys, cast us off. Walt, all aboard! Erin, this is because of you. Do you realize that? You're the best ever!

q: In “The Whale”, who turns out to be the buyer behind the huge Scranton White Pages account?
why: Jan had expected David Wallace to show up, and Dwight ended up offering her young Clark as her “personal Dunder Mifflin liaison.”

cite.t: Oh my God. It's Jan.

q: In “The Target”, who is the target of the man Angela hires through Dwight?
why: Angela had worked out that Oscar was sleeping with her husband, and Dwight’s friend Trevor planned a knee-capping with a lead pipe.

cite.t: You hired someone to hit me with a pipe!

q: In “Dwight Christmas”, which Christmas figure does Dwight dress up as for his Pennsylvania Dutch party?
why: As Belsnickel, Dwight judges people “impish” or “admirable”: Phyllis is admirable and gets rubber gaskets for canning jars, while Oscar and Jim are impish and get hit with his stick.

cite.t: What about an authentic Pennsylvania Dutch Christmas? Drink some gluhwein, enjoy some hasenpfeffer. Enjoy Christmas with saint Nicolas' rural German companion, Belsnickel.

q: In “Lice”, who really brought the lice into the office while Meredith takes the blame?
why: Pam had caught it from Cece and let the office blame Meredith, who shaved her head, until everyone heard Pam’s mom on the phone saying Cece still had lice.

cite.t: Maybe it was Meredith. Maybe she brought in lice that are totally different than the lice that i got from Cece. So let's not jump to the simplest conclusion that she got her lice from me. That is how wars get started. Fine, I'll tell her it was me.

q: In “Suit Warehouse”, what does Dwight ask Clark to pretend to be to land the sale?
why: The client ran a father-and-son suit store, and Dwight switched to a bad-relationship act once the owner admitted his own son hated his guts.

cite.t: How would you like to pretend to by my son in order to land a sale?

q: In “Customer Loyalty”, who steps in to comfort Pam after her phone fight with Jim?
why: When a cameraman calls his name, Brian tells him to give her a minute, then tells the crew to turn the cameras off.

cite.t: Nothing. You're doing the best you can.

q: In “Junior Salesman”, who ends up at Jim’s desk as the new junior sales associate?
why: Dwight stacked the interviews with buddies like Rolf, who goes fishing with hand grenades. When they flopped, he got Jim to turn them all down, and Jim picked Clark instead.

cite.t: Oh, cool. Hey Clark.

q: In “Vandalism”, what does Frank from the warehouse paint over Pam’s mural?
why: Pam struck back by painting Frank’s truck with a picture of him leaving a trail of poops, using water-based paint.

cite.t: I'm sorry I didn't like your crappy doodles. I drew a butt. Big deal. Butts are funny.

q: In “Couples Discount”, what does Erin end up doing after Andy comes home early from his boat trip?
why: She did it while David Wallace was still on the line with Andy, so Wallace heard that Andy had been gone for three months.

cite.t: We're breaking up. And just so you know, I was worried that you were dead. You were gone for three months.

q: In “Moving On”, who does Dwight recruit Angela to help him take care of?
why: Dwight said she needed “a woman’s touch,” and Angela refused to hose her down like an animal, insisting on a proper bath and a haircut instead.

cite.t: It's my aunt Shirley, she's on her last legs.

q: In “The Farm”, what does Dwight’s brother Jeb actually grow on his nine-acre farm?
why: Jeb bought what he thought was a worm farm from a Californian, and Dwight was disgusted he hadn’t grown something like a peanut-grape hybrid instead.

cite.t: I can't stand the fact that Jeb is a pot farmer. He could've grown anything. Anything in the world. He used to talk about growing a peanut-grape hybrid. One plant, one sandwhich.

q: In the “Promos” cold open, which audiobook has Phyllis getting a little too worked up at her desk?
why: Toby said she was allowed to feel aroused at work as long as she didn’t act on it, so Dwight stepped in himself and Andy confiscated it until the end of the day.

cite.t: She's listening to 50 Shades of Grey.

q: In “Stairmageddon”, how does Dwight get Stanley out to a sales call while the elevator is down?
a: Shoots him with a tranquilizer dart
why: The dose was meant for “a very small bull,” and a woozy Stanley still closed a sale with one of the branch’s biggest clients.

cite.t: Don't worry, it's just a bull tranquilizer. Nothing to be alarmed about. It's just a man pointing a bull tranquilizer at a coworker.

q: In “Paper Airplane”, who wins the office paper airplane contest and its $2,000 prize?
why: Dwight tried to tank the final so the newly broke Angela would get the money, but she told him not to dare, after Toby had crumpled his own plane to let her through the semi-final.

cite.t: And we have a winner. And it's Dwight. And it is everyone because this is over.

q: In “Livin’ the Dream”, why does Andy quit Dunder Mifflin?
why: David Wallace had come in planning to fire him over the boat trip and a head shot printer, but Andy cut him off and quit first.

cite.t: Well, no, actually. I see no reason to limit myself to just acting. I am pursuing fame of any kind. Could be singing, could be dancing. I don't--it just... I owe it to myself and my future fans.

q: In “A.A.R.M.”, what does Angela confess right after accepting Dwight’s roadside proposal?
why: She had lied because she needed Dwight to want to marry her for her own sake, and his answer was “Get out! I’m a dad!”

cite.t: Phillip's your son.

q: In “Finale”, who does Jim secretly bring in to stand beside Dwight at his wedding?
why: Jim called it the “best prank ever,” and Michael greeted Dwight with one last “That’s what she said.”

cite.t: Michael. I can't believe you came.

q: In “Finale”, what got Kevin fired by Dwight?
why: Dwight fired him with a cake frosted “Get out,” and Kevin later bought a bar.

cite.t: That's the reason Kevin got fired. It's his magic number. He used to use it to balance his accounts. He used to call it a Keleven. He told Dwight, "A mistake plus Keleven gets you home by seven." He was home by 4

q: In “Finale”, what did Creed do the day after the documentary aired?
a: Faked his death in the baler
w: Fled to Canada on a bus
Hid out on a fishing boat
why: The stunt only fooled Kevin, and the police went on to reveal Creed’s 1960s past in the band The Grass Roots.

cite.t: I brought in some new faces, and one old. I always like Devon. I hired him back after Creed faked his own death in the baler the day after the doc aired. The only person he fooled was Kevin. Then the police showed up. Turns out, Creed was in the band "The Grass Roots" in the 1960's. During that time, the police say he sold drugs and trafficked in endangered species meat and stole weapons-grade LSD from the military.
